label: D2 candidate: strongly negative after rare a1->S2, high after a2->S1
terms: (phase == D2) * (action == 1) * (state == 2) ;; (phase == D2) * (action == 2) * (state == 1) ;; (phase == D2) * (action == 1) * (state == 1) ;; (phase == D1) * (prev_action == 1) * (prev_reward == 0) ;; (phase == D2) * (prev_action == 1) ;; (phase == D2) * (prev_reward == 0) ;; (phase == GO) * (prev_reward == 0)
explanation: Raw candidate n of unit 35 sits near +1 at D1/GO and drops at D2 with episode time (timing R^2 0.47). Beyond timing, the magnitude is driven mainly by the just-made choice x reached state at D2 (all observed at D2): a1 reaching S2 (rare) pushes it strongly negative (about -0.8), a2 reaching S1 (rare) raises it (+0.46), a1->S1 raises it moderately (+0.24), a2->S2 is the reference. Smaller history effects: lower at D2 when the previous choice was a1 or the previous trial was unrewarded, and lower at D1/GO after an unrewarded trial (especially after a1 unrewarded at D1). Hidden good state, since-reversal and value add little. Adding the model policy logit at D2 raises dev R^2 beyond timing from 0.76 to 0.81, but it is not recorded. Observed-only, 7 terms: dev R^2 beyond timing 0.76; all-cue ceiling 0.90, all observed 0.80.

issues: The main claim holds. The D2 choice x state effect reproduces on test: a1->S2 -0.82, a2->S1 +0.49, a1->S1 +0.27, with a2->S2 as the reference. The 7 terms give test R^2 beyond timing 0.750. The choice x state reference table alone gives 0.71, so almost all of the explained variance comes from this one effect.

The history claim 'n is lower at D2 when the previous choice was a1' (weight -0.146) is mostly a misattribution. Adding the term (phase==D2)*(action==2)*(state==2)*(prev_action==1) gives that switch case a weight of -0.54. The diffuse prev_action main effect then shrinks to -0.04. So the real effect is that a2->S2 is much lower right after an a1 trial (a switch from a1 to a2 that lands in S2). It is not a general effect of having chosen a1 last.

The claim 'n is lower at D2 after an unrewarded trial' is too coarse. The D2 profile residuals are a1 S2 r -0.002 vs a1 S2 u -0.365, but a1 S1 r -0.153 vs a1 S1 u -0.16. So the reward effect depends on which state was reached. A term for the previous trial being S2 and unrewarded (weight -0.20) replaces the plain prev_reward==0 term and fits better.

misses on the recorded terms shows systematic D2 errors by previous trial: after a2 S1 u under-predicted by +0.158, after a1 S2 u over-predicted by -0.100, after a2 S2 u over-predicted by -0.067. GO after a1 S2 u is also off by -0.06 to -0.10. The worst windows are runs of late-episode a2->S2c D2 steps with n near -0.8 where the model predicts about 0 to +0.3, most of them after a1 trials or unrewarded S2 visits.

With a term budget of 8, history terms that depend on the state reached (and on switching) raise test R^2 beyond timing from 0.750 to 0.782, against an observed-only ceiling of 0.80. The original terms leave about 60% of the reachable observed-only gap unexplained.

No future variables are used, which is correct. The claim that the hidden good state adds little checks out (+0.009 on test). The policy logit at D2 adds about +0.05 (test 0.799), which suggests the remaining structure is evidence about which state is good, built up from state x reward history.
